frontmatter.title: Crustless Spinach & Gruyère Quiche
ingredients: 1/2 cup Plain Greek Yogurt for richness

exactBefore.body:
## Chef's Note

This French-style quiche sautés onions over high heat until edges char and caramelize, adding smokiness that balances earthy spinach. Greek yogurt replaces heavy cream for a firmer, protein-rich custard that doesn't turn watery. Gruyère's nutty flavor is more complex than standard Swiss cheese.

## Directions

1.  **The Blacken:** In a large skillet, heat oil over high heat. Add the sliced onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply browned and slightly charred at the edges.
2.  **The Wilt:** Add the spinach to the onions. Toss for 1 minute until just wilted. **Discard any excess liquid** from the pan.
3.  **The Custard:** In a medium bowl, whisk together the eggs, Greek yogurt, salt, and pepper until perfectly smooth.
4.  **Fold:** Stir the onion-spinach mixture and 3/4 of the Gruyère into the egg custard.
5.  **Bake:** Preheat oven to 350°F. Spray a 9-inch pie plate with oil. Pour the mixture into the plate and sprinkle the remaining cheese over the top.
6.  **Finish:** Bake for 25-30 minutes until the top is golden brown and the center is set.
7.  **Serve:** Serve warm or at room temperature with a side of greens.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Coat a 9-inch pie plate with {{ingredients}}. Choose a plate deep enough for the full filling below its rim; prepare an extra small oven-safe dish if necessary.

steps.title: Brown the onion deeply
steps.text: Heat {{ingredients}} in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Cook, stirring often and adjusting the heat, until the onion softens and becomes deeply browned with a few charred edges. Start checking after about 5 minutes and allow roughly 8–12 minutes; avoid a black, bitter layer on the bottom of the pan.

steps.title: Cook the spinach without leaving water
steps.text: Add {{ingredients}} in handfuls as space becomes available. Toss until fully wilted, then keep cooking until free moisture has evaporated. If a large puddle remains, drain the cooked vegetables in a sieve, pressing gently without discarding vegetables. Spread the vegetables out and let them cool until only warm before mixing with the eggs.

steps.title: Mix the eggs and seasoning
steps.text: Whisk {{ingredients}} just until evenly blended; there is no need to beat in a thick foam.

steps.title: Mix in the cheese and vegetables
steps.text: Stir {{ingredients}} and all the cooled onion-spinach mixture into the eggs. Spread the full filling evenly in the prepared plate, keeping it below the rim. Put any excess in the extra coated dish rather than forcing the plate full.

steps.title: Bake by the center
steps.text: Bake at 350°F, beginning the first check around 25 minutes; about 25–40 minutes is a planning range. The top should be lightly browned and the center fully set, with no liquid egg movement. Measure at least 160°F in the central egg filling, keeping the sensing part of the thermometer away from the pan. Check any extra dish separately. Depth, starting temperature and oven heat can require longer.

steps.title: Rest briefly, then serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes before slicing. Serve warm with a fresh salad. Refrigerate remaining portions within 2 hours of cooking, or 1 hour above 90°F, while still warm if needed.

learning.focus: Brown the onion, remove spinach moisture and set the eggs gently.
learning.outcome: A tender, sliceable egg filling with sweet browned onion, nutty Gruyère and no puddle of spinach water.
before: Use the full listed spinach, eggs and Gruyère; freshly grate the cheese.
Choose a 9-inch plate with room below its rim for the filling; have a small extra dish ready if needed.
Cook the spinach thoroughly and let the vegetables cool to warm before folding them into the eggs.

checkpoints.cue: The onion is soft and deeply browned, with scattered charred edges.
checkpoints.why: This preserves the original blackened-onion character without a bitter burned layer.

checkpoints.cue: The spinach is fully wilted and there is no free puddle in the vegetables.
checkpoints.why: Excess vegetable water would collect around the set egg.

checkpoints.cue: The middle is set with no liquid egg, and the central filling reaches at least 160°F.
checkpoints.why: A golden top alone does not establish a cooked center.

troubleshooting.cause: The spinach or cooked onions retained too much free liquid.
troubleshooting.fix: Cook or drain the vegetables until no puddle remains before mixing. Do not fix this by dropping spinach from the formula.

troubleshooting.problem: The edges become rubbery before the center sets.
troubleshooting.cause: The filling is too deep or the oven runs hot.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the center and keep baking only as needed; shield a darkening top. Use enough suitably sized vessels for the full batch next time.

learning.storage: After serving, refrigerate in shallow portions at 40°F or below within 2 hours of cooking, or 1 hour above 90°F; refrigerate while still warm if necessary rather than waiting on the counter for full cooling. Cover once cool and use within 3–4 days, including any earlier refrigerated storage of cooked vegetables. Reheat leftovers to 165°F in the center, lightly covered to limit drying. For longer storage, freeze cooled portions promptly; thaw in the refrigerator. Keep the same remaining storage deadline after reheating.
learning.timing: Preparation includes browning the onion, wilting and draining the spinach, and cooling the vegetables briefly. Allow about 25–40 minutes baking after mixing, followed by 10 minutes rest; continue until the center checks are satisfied. When scaling, keep all filling ratios together and choose enough appropriately sized vessels; do not multiply pan diameter, oven temperature or bake time. For a fractional egg quantity, beat an egg and weigh out the required fraction rather than rounding the egg count.

exactAfter.body:
## Chef's Note

Rebecca’s crustless spinach quiche pairs browned onion with nutty Gruyère. Cook the spinach until its free water is gone, then fold the warm vegetables into the eggs and cheese. Let the center set gently and rest the quiche before slicing.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the baking dish:** Heat the oven to 350°F. Coat a 9-inch pie plate with cooking spray. Choose a plate deep enough for the full filling below its rim; prepare an extra small oven-safe dish if necessary.
2. **Brown the onion deeply:** Heat olive oil and large yellow onion in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Cook, stirring often and adjusting the heat, until the onion softens and becomes deeply browned with a few charred edges. Start checking after about 5 minutes and allow roughly 8–12 minutes; avoid a black, bitter layer on the bottom of the pan.
3. **Cook the spinach without leaving water:** Add fresh baby spinach in handfuls as space becomes available. Toss until fully wilted, then keep cooking until free moisture has evaporated. If a large puddle remains, drain the cooked vegetables in a sieve, pressing gently without discarding vegetables. Spread the vegetables out and let them cool until only warm before mixing with the eggs.
4. **Mix the eggs and seasoning:** Whisk large eggs, fine sea salt, and ground black pepper just until evenly blended; there is no need to beat in a thick foam.
5. **Mix in the cheese and vegetables:** Stir Gruyère cheese and all the cooled onion-spinach mixture into the eggs. Spread the full filling evenly in the prepared plate, keeping it below the rim. Put any excess in the extra coated dish rather than forcing the plate full.
6. **Bake by the center:** Bake at 350°F, beginning the first check around 25 minutes; about 25–40 minutes is a planning range. The top should be lightly browned and the center fully set, with no liquid egg movement. Measure at least 160°F in the central egg filling, keeping the sensing part of the thermometer away from the pan. Check any extra dish separately. Depth, starting temperature and oven heat can require longer.
7. **Rest briefly, then serve:** Rest for 10 minutes before slicing. Serve warm with a fresh salad. Refrigerate remaining portions within 2 hours of cooking, or 1 hour above 90°F, while still warm if needed.

findings.scope: Whole recipe with disclosed source-versus-adaptation choices
findings.exactBeforeAfter: See exactBefore and exactAfter for complete cooking text and all changed fields
rationale: Rebecca’s transmitted original contains one onion, 10 oz spinach, six eggs and unquantified Gruyère; neither cream nor yogurt is present.

One cup Gruyère, large egg/onion sizes, olive oil, measured fine sea salt/pepper and fresh baby spinach are retained contemporary current specifications, not recovered family measurements. All original spinach/egg quantities and the blackened-onion identity remain.
All cheese is mixed with the vegetables and eggs, following the original full mixing route instead of carrying the later three-quarter/one-quarter topping allocation.

The half-cup yogurt is omitted from the main, not described as replacing original cream. FAGE’s full yogurt quiche uses materially different yogurt/egg/cheese amounts and does not establish a beneficial change to Rebecca’s formula. No yogurt variation is certified.
Six portions is the current planning yield within the original 6–8 range, not a weighed kitchen yield.
